rules.text: Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Has the patient ever had kidney/upper urinary tract stones (symptomatic event or incidentally detected stone)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient a child (<18 years of age)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the child toilet-trained (so that a 24-hour urine collection is feasible)?. Recommendation: Perform an in-depth metabolic evaluation including at least one (preferably two) 24-hour urine collections plus serum tests; manage as pediatric stone former with multidisciplinary Urology and Nephrology involvement, focusing on increased fluid intake (70–100 ml/kg/day), sodium reduction, and targeted pharmacologic therapy as needed.

rules.text: Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Has the patient ever had kidney/upper urinary tract stones (symptomatic event or incidentally detected stone)? rules.text: Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Has the patient ever had kidney/upper urinary tract stones (symptomatic event or incidentally detected stone)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient a child (<18 years of age)? AND The answer must be YES: Is this the patient’s first known stone episode (no prior stones known or documented)? AND The answer must be YES: Does the patient have any listed high-risk features for recurrent stone disease (e.g., bilateral/multiple stones, non-calcium or pure calcium phosphate stone, complicated episode with AKI/sepsis/hospitalization, solitary kidney, renal insufficiency, systemic stone-promoting disease, high-risk occupation, family history)?. Recommendation: Perform an in-depth metabolic evaluation (serum panel, at least one and preferably two 24-hour urine collections, dietary history) and institute individualized dietary and pharmacologic prevention according to identified abnormalities and stone type.
